title: Margo's Ground Rules

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: My quarter, my rules: buy something at every third stall, argue about the price, and never point.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: The stalls each have a call. Tonight you find things by listening. Asking gets reported.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: The Lantern Quarter on market night: paper light, vendor calls in her grandmother's tongue, and one stall that is quieter than it should be.

caseLine: Friday, the Lantern Quarter. Find the Lattice Stall without asking for it.

title: The Masked Meeting

lines.speaker: ottilie
lines.en: Go home, little wren. Some paintings prefer to be lost.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: A voice behind the lattice screen: polite, older, unhurried. Grey gloves at the screen's edge. She knows the first name nobody uses. Then the drop goes silent forever.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: You hear it? The Nachtigall — the nightingale. In Oma's stories she sings only where she cannot be seen.

caseLine: Found the drop. The Broker knows my name — the small one.

peopleFacts.fact: Voice: older, polite. Knows Halloway's first name. The market shields her.

title: Margo's Wobble

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: My editor wants the museum-negligence story tonight. Printing it scatters the market — and the Broker with it.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: So I sit on it. On the record: I hate this beautifully.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: Her cost buys tonight's access. Allies stay clean in Marlowe Bay; they just don't stay comfortable.

caseLine: Margo sits on her story. The cost is hers; the access is ours.

peopleFacts.fact: Sat on the negligence story to protect the trail. It cost her.

title: Rails Go Two Directions

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: Who rides a freight tram at a quarter past eleven? Nobody with a clean conscience or a warm coat.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: The depot keeps every waybill. The dispatcher communicates by thermos and pointing, and his lost signal-lamp key is on your list.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: Nothing up Clocktower Lane but pigeons and the old chart rooms. — Pigeons don't sign waybills, Halloway.

caseLine: Oct 11, 23:15: unscheduled freight to Clocktower Lane. Retired-staff pass No. 7.

title: The Loft at Dawn

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: 6 Kestrel Lane, top floor, tenant 'away'. Pinholes, pounce-dust, artificially aged varnish. A copyist's studio — meticulous, left-handed, and gone.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: My abuela said: the house talks if nobody shouts. So — shh.

caseLine: The Daughter was pounced — copied full-size — in this room.

peopleFacts.fact: 'E. Sarto': meticulous, away, no signatures anywhere.

title: Dead Men Don't Buy Linseed

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: The green: ground copper-resinate in beeswax, labeled in a steady old hand matching the 1904 materials note. Left-hand wear on everything.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: Dead men don't buy linseed, Halloway.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: Two teacups, washed, on the drying rack. One resident. Two cups. Nobody says so.

caseLine: The copyist grinds Vane's green, letters like Vane, works left-handed. Vane's hand lives.

peopleFacts.fact: The recipe is his. The lettering is his. The hand is left.
